extracted.intended_audience: general public / researchers / journalists seeking an overview of BP's controversies
extracted.subtask_description: A descriptive summary of BP's environmental, safety, legal, and political controversies, incidents, and regulatory findings drawn from a Wikipedia-style company-criticism article. Covers accidents, regulatory actions, rankings, investigations, and settlements.

rubrics_metrics.name: AERI indigenous-rights ranking criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: The Arctic Environmental Responsibility Index ranking 'took into account 20 criteria, such as the companies' commitments to international standards, the presence of organisational units dedicated to handling indigenous rights, competent staffing, track records on indigenous issues, transparency, and procedures for consulting with indigenous peoples, but the actual performance of companies on indigenous rights was not assessed.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rubric assesses corporate commitments and organisational capacity for indigenous-rights issues (policy commitments, dedicated units, staffing, transparency, consultation procedures), but does not necessarily evaluate on-the-ground performance. Use the 20-criteria framework for comparative ranking; note limitation that actual performance may not be measured.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refinery air-quality compliance (AQMD standards)
rubrics_metrics.description: Alleged violations: BP/ARCO was accused of illegally releasing air pollutants 'by failing to adequately inspect, maintain, repair and properly operate thousands of pieces of equipment across the refinery as required by AQMD regulations.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation focuses on adherence to local air-quality agency rules: timely inspection, maintenance, repair, and proper operation of equipment. Enforcement outcomes (complaints, civil penalties, settlements) and remedial commitments (cash penalties, funding for environmental improvements and community programs) are relevant measures of compliance and remediation.

rubrics_metrics.name: OSHA / process-safety management and organisational safety expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: OSHA citations included failures such as 'locating people in vulnerable buildings among the processing units, failing to correct depressurisation deficiencies and deficiencies with gas monitors, and failing to prevent the use of non-approved electrical equipment' and management failures 'neglecting to develop shutdown procedures and designate responsibilities and to establish a system to promptly address and resolve recommendations made after an incident.' Specific PSM failures: 'failure to develop operating procedures for a unit that removes sulphur compound; failure to ensure that operating procedures reflect current operating practice in the Isocracker Unit; failure to resolve process hazard analysis recommendations; failure to resolve process safety management compliance audit items in a timely manner; and failure to periodically inspect pressure piping systems.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessments should examine both technical/process controls (PHAs, device/monitoring maintenance, piping inspections) and organisational systems (clear shutdown procedures, responsibility assignment, audit-followup mechanisms). Repeated or systemic failures increase severity; OSHA fines and findings of 'systemic safety problem' are indicators of organisational-level deficiencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pipeline inspection and maintenance standards (use of inspection 'pigs' and corrosion prevention)
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulatory expectation illustrated by Prudhoe Bay: 'pipeline inspection gauges (known as "pigs") had not been run through the pipeline since 1998.' Regulators ordered inspection using 'smart pigs' and issued Corrective Action Orders requiring pipeline repair or replacement; consent decree required measures 'to significantly improve inspection and maintenance of its pipeline infrastructure' and imposed a civil penalty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate pipeline integrity programs by frequency and quality of in-line inspections (smart pigs), prompt remediation of detected corrosion/thinning, and compliance with corrective-action orders. Failure to run inspections or to act on findings is a major compliance deficiency and leads to enforcement and financial penalties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory compliance with Clean Water Act, Clean Air Act, and Pipeline Safety Act
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple enforcement actions cited: BP Exploration, Alaska pleaded guilty to negligent discharge under the Clean Water Act and was fined; BP pleaded guilty to a felony Clean Air Act charge related to the Texas City refinery and was fined and sentenced to probation; complaints alleged violations of the Clean Water Act, Clean Air Act and the Pipeline Safety Act in other instances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rubric: companies must comply with federal environmental statutes; violations can lead to criminal guilty pleas, civil penalties, consent decrees, probation, and mandated remedial measures. Assess legal outcomes (guilty pleas, fines, consent decrees) as evidence of statutory noncompliance and remedial obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Worker safety and protective-equipment/safety-procedure expectations for cleanup and operations
rubrics_metrics.description: Reports indicate 'cleanup workers were not provided safety equipment by the company, and the safety manuals were "rarely if ever" followed, or distributed to workers.' Manuals advised 'Avoid breathing vapor' and 'Wear suitable protective clothing.' Workers reported they 'were not allowed to use respirators.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether employers provide appropriate PPE, training, and enforce safety manuals. Failure to supply PPE or to follow manuals is both a safety and liability failing; public-health studies detecting biomarkers or increased disease risk among exposed workers support evaluations of inadequate protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental impact-assessment (EIA) accessibility and adequacy for affected communities
rubrics_metrics.description: In the Ocensa pipeline case, most land traversed was owned by peasant farmers 'who were illiterate and unable to read the environmental impact assessment conducted by BP prior to construction, which acknowledged significant and widespread risks of damage to the land.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess EIA quality both for technical completeness (identifying risks to soil, groundwater, crops, livestock) and for accessibility/consultation practices (readability, informed consent, outreach to illiterate or vulnerable stakeholders). A compliant EIA should be accompanied by meaningful consultation and accessible disclosures to affected communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corporate transparency and information dissemination (to partners, regulators, public)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples of 'exceptionally circumspect in disseminating information' (Caspian Sea blowout) and accusations of misleading investors about flow rates in Deepwater Horizon litigation and withholding information even from partners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rubric measures timeliness, completeness and candour of disclosures to partners, regulators, and the public. Secretive or delayed disclosure can trigger investigations, partner complaints, regulatory action, and reputational/legal consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Market-trading compliance and anti-manipulation standards (CFTC/FERC/Court expectations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Allegations and actions included: charges that BP traders conspired to 'raise the price of propane by seeking to corner the propane market'; pleas/guilty pleas by former traders; payments of restitution and fines; CFTC and FERC investigations into attempted market manipulation and alleged fraudulent trading in gas markets; and civil penalties and compliance/monitoring requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess commodity trading by adherence to anti-manipulation law (Commodity Exchange Act), market reporting accuracy, and internal compliance programs. Remedial actions include fines, restitution, implementation of compliance/ethics programs, and court-appointed monitors. Repeated enforcement suggests insufficient controls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency between corporate climate/low-carbon commitments and actual investment/activity (greenwashing risk)
rubrics_metrics.description: Accusations that BP (and other majors) engaged in 'greenwashing' Paris Agreement pledges while continuing long-term investment in fossil fuel production and sales; BP set targets (e.g., reduce oil/gas production by 40% by 2030) then reportedly scrapped or lowered ambitions, and later increased fossil-fuel investment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate credibility of climate commitments by comparing announced targets and public statements to capital-allocation, investment decisions, production plans, and lobbying/communications. Indicators of greenwashing include large pledges without matching investment shifts, reductions in ambition, or simultaneous promotion of fossil fuels as 'bridge' fuels.
